title: Number of ZigZag Arrays III
summary: Given integers n, l, and r, calculate the count of ZigZag arrays of length n where each element is within [l, r], no two adjacent elements are the same, and no three consecutive elements form a strictly increasing or decreasing sequence.
statement: Given integers n, l, and r, calculate the count of ZigZag arrays of length n where each element is within [l, r], no two adjacent elements are the same, and no three consecutive elements form a strictly increasing or decreasing sequence. Return the count modulo 10^9 + 7.
constraints: Every value lies in [l,r], adjacent values differ, and three consecutive values may not be strictly monotone.
reference_solution:
def count_zigzag_arrays(n,l,r):
    modulus=1_000_000_007;width=r-l+1
    if n==1:return width
    up=[value for value in range(width)];down=[width-1-value for value in range(width)]
    for _ in range(2,n):
        prefix=[];running=0
        for value in down:running=(running+value)%modulus;prefix.append(running)
        suffix=[0]*width;running=0
        for i in range(width-1,-1,-1):running=(running+up[i])%modulus;suffix[i]=running
        up=[prefix[i-1] if i else 0 for i in range(width)]
        down=[suffix[i+1] if i+1<width else 0 for i in range(width)]
    return (sum(up)+sum(down))%modulus

hints: After two elements, validity depends only on the last value and whether the last comparison went up or down.
An up step must follow a down step from a smaller value; a down step symmetrically follows an up step from a larger value.
Prefix and suffix sums evaluate all strict predecessor ranges in linear time per position.
Alternating comparison directions are exactly the condition excluding equal neighbors and monotone triples.
